ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows an npn transistor, with the emitter below and grounded; the collector is above and connected to an external terminal; the base is led out from the left side, and is short-circuited with the node where the collector is located through the left-side wire. Therefore this transistor is in the diode-connected form with the base and collector short-circuited. The figure also marks V_BE, as well as the direction of the collector current I_C. Then reason: Since the base and collector are short-circuited, it can be treated as a diode-connected transistor, mainly considering the forward-biased base-emitter junction. Given V_BE = 0.7 V, reverse saturation current I_S = 10^{-13} A, temperature T = 300 K. At room temperature, the thermal voltage V_T = kT/q ≈ 0.026 V. From the diode equation: I_E ≈ I_S(e^{V_BE/V_T} - 1). Substituting the values: I_E ≈ 10^{-13}(e^{0.7/0.026} - 1) A. Because 0.7/0.026 ≈ 26.92, e^{26.92} ≈ 4.9 × 10^{11}, so I_E ≈ 10^{-13} × 4.9 × 10^{11} A = 4.9 × 10^{-2} A = 49 mA.
